title: Lithuania Faces Twin Pressures as Defence Ambitions Collide with Fiscal… · 10 Oct
keywords: Lithuania, defence spending, fiscal deficit, NATO, EU fiscal rules, labour shortage, foreign workers, migration policy, Baltic states, economic growth, inflation, European Commission, public finances, eastern flank
notes: Lithuania is planning to raise defence spending to more than 5% of GDP by 2027, a move that would push its budget deficit above the European Union's reference threshold. At the same time, new restrictions on foreign workers are threatening to choke off a labour supply that businesses say has driven nearly half of the country's economic growth over the past five years. Together, the two debates expose the central dilemma facing one of NATO's most exposed member states: how to build security and regulate migration without undermining the economy that funds both.
